title: Rural living; schooling and business college
description: Anna Brebner tells Dale Anderson why she prefers rural life in St. Mary's over town. She discusses her siblings' education, including a sister who studied music, and her own year and a half at a Spokane business college learning bookkeeping, typing, and shorthand.

title: Courtship and marriage; Miltown and the mill
description: Anna recounts her courtship with Jim beginning in high school in 1912 while her family lived in Miltown near the lumber mill, where they walked the railroad tracks. Jim served in World War I, and after his return they married in 1920 and went back to Montana.

title: Children; childbirth and family doctors
description: Anna describes wanting and raising seven children, all born in the St. Mary's hospital with Dr. Cornwall as the longtime family doctor. She says she raised them by instinct, did not push them in schoolwork, and is pleased with how her children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren are doing.

title: Travel and vacations; family origins
description: Anna explains that family trips have mostly been to visit relatives in North Bend, California, and Coeur d'Alene rather than sightseeing. She recalls her childhood in Wisconsin, her husband's family, and traveling by bus, car, and plane.

title: Trains and steamboats; world's fairs
description: Anna fondly remembers passenger trains through St. Mary's and riding paddle-wheel steamboats like the Georgie Oaks from Coeur d'Alene up the river. She also compares the Seattle and Spokane world's fairs, preferring Spokane's.

title: Recreation; housework and baking
description: Now less active, Anna describes outings, family gatherings, and looking at a book of old riverboats. She details her daily homemaking routine of baking bread weekly, making pies and cookies, and corresponding with family by cassette tape.

title: Town growth; the family land
description: Anna talks about old friends and the changes in St. Mary's as the plywood plant and railroad brought many newcomers, which she sees as good for the town. She recounts buying their land in 1938 and settling on the farm as a good place to raise children.

title: Canning and food storage; church and clubs
description: Anna describes canning applesauce, freezing fruit and vegetables, and keeping a big freezer. She then discusses her church involvement, mission sewing work, the deanery of Catholic women, and the Grandmothers' Club.

title: Travel wishes; embroidery and needlework
description: Anna says she would have liked to see more of the country but now only visits people she knows. She describes her lifelong embroidery, tatting, crocheting, and knitting, including an award-winning county fair entry, and which daughters carry on such crafts.

title: Religion and the Catholic school
description: Anna explains that her husband converted to Catholicism and that church has always been central to her life. She recalls attending Catholic school in Coeur d'Alene and that all her children attended the Catholic grade school in St. Mary's and remain Catholic.

title: The boarding house; Depression and wars
description: After deflecting requests for advice, Anna describes helping at her mother's boarding house waiting tables. She recounts hard times during the Depression eased by keeping a cow, pigs, chickens, and a garden, and her family's experiences in both world wars.

title: Garden food and hunting; reading
description: Anna details how the garden, frozen vegetables, and venison and elk from their son supply much of their food. She finishes by describing her magazine subscriptions and the talking-book service she uses because of her failing eyesight.

title: Book tastes; television programmes; no movie theatre in St. Mary's
description: Anna Brebner tells Dale Anderson that she still prefers older, homey books by writers like Kathleen Norris, and lists the kinds of books now available to her. She describes her television habits, naming shows such as the Waltons, Lawrence Welk, What's My Line and Disney, and says St. Mary's has lacked a movie house for years because the former owners blocked competition, though an outdoor cinema has been tried at Plummer.

title: Home baking; marital decision-making; family planning
description: Dale Anderson asks what her husband asks her about and Anna answers that he asks what kind of pie she made. She explains that she makes pies, puddings, cakes and white bread from scratch, and that her grandchildren love her plain rolls. She says big decisions were made jointly with her husband and that their children were not planned but just came along.

title: Mother's business career; comparing their lives
description: Anna compares her life with her mother's, describing her mother as a talented businesswoman who ran the Kootenai Inn, a confectionery store on Main Street and another store in Davenport, Washington, and later bought a property in St. Mary's. Anna thinks she herself is happier than her mother was and says she would never have wanted that kind of work.

title: Mother's working life; upbringing in Coeur d'Alene and St. Mary's; staying home
description: Anna explains how her mother combined work with raising children, recalling time in Coeur d'Alene where her aunt ran a boarding house for the Blackwell mill and where Anna and her sister worked in the dining room yet still had nice clothes and schooling. She says her mother's work had no bad effect on her, and that the only paid work she ever did was bookkeeping at her mother's inn, having always been content at home.
